body: This PR has the label `held-for-merge`. The maintainer merges it. No agent merges it. PR B of #917 will stack on this PR.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 647d37204f1fca4e1bce065a0f4a8ef5cc0a0c06 -->
Read-only review (Opus). Not built here.

**Verdict: Needs changes before merge.** One blocker. The other items are sound. The notes below are not blockers.

### Blocker

1. `crates/kernel/src/machining_mesh.rs:271-284` (the inward turn). The turn uses the signed volume of the full mesh. It turns all triangles. The solidcore record can have more than one shell in a region (`Region { shells, void }`, see `solidcore_trims.rs:294-297`). Example: the outer shell points inward and a void shell points correctly into the void. The total volume is `-(Vo + Vv)`, which is negative. The PR turns all triangles. Then the void shell points the wrong direction, the volume reads `Vo + Vv`, and the mesh passes. Before this PR, the same input was refused (`Volume`). Under the safety floor, an input that changes from "refused" to "accepted with a wrong cavity and a wrong volume" is not permitted.
   - Do this: turn the mesh only when it is one connected shell (count the components of the welded triangles, or read the record's shell count). For more than one shell, keep the `Volume` refusal. Alternatively, decide the turn for each shell by its nesting. That is more work.
   - Add a pin: a two-shell box with a void, outer shell turned, void correct, must stay refused (or must come out correct).

### Checked and sound

- **Adaptive bound (`mesh_deviation.rs:207-271`).** `dmax + longest side` is a true upper bound for the measured direction (mesh point to surface). Each corner `d` is `|p - S(q)|` for a real surface point, so `d >= dist(p, S)`. The distance to a set is 1-Lipschitz, and each point of a flat triangle is within the longest side of a corner. The `min` can only lower a bound to this true bound. It cannot go below it.
- **Caps.** The depth cap (12) and the budget (`*budget >= 3` before `*budget -= 3`, so no underflow) stop the refinement and return the bound of that node. That bound is conservative. A budget that is empty for a later face gives more refusals, never fewer. The recursion depth is at most 12. The recursion allocates nothing. The cancel token is read at each split. Termination is correct.
- **Changed pins.** The readings are 8.7e-9 mm, 5.95e-8 mm and 1.98e-7 mm under the tolerance. A reading just under the tolerance is what an adaptive refinement gives: it stops when the bound is at or under the tolerance. It is not a float artefact. The float error of the bound is about 1e-13 mm on these coordinates. All three readings are honest proofs. See note 1 for the one error source that the comparison does not include.
- **Snap (`mesh_weld.rs:768-775`).** `c - g` is exact (Sterbenz) when `c` is near `g`, so the window test is exact and no coordinate moves more than 1e-9 mm. Each vertex moves at most `sqrt(3) * 1e-9` mm. Two vertices merge only when each axis differs by at most 2e-9 mm. Two vertices that are 1e-6 mm apart cannot merge. Equal inputs give equal outputs, so the snap never opens a weld that the old exact weld made. NaN, infinity and `|k| > 9e15` stay unchanged. A dropped collapsed facet that opens a hole leaves a side used once, and `sides()` refuses it before the volume step.
- **Spline guard (`step_curve_guard.rs`).** The left and right control point indices are correct for a knot with multiplicity above the degree (The NURBS Book). The index math cannot overflow: `points.get(start - 1)` must succeed first, so `start` is small. A NaN or zero weight is refused.
- **Solid ranges.** `Mesh::from_solids` refuses ranges that do not tile the facets. `slice_of` refuses a range out of bounds and keeps the soup refusal for an inward solid.
- **Test location.** The snap is in `camcraft_kernel`, so its pins in `crates/kernel/tests/machining_mesh_parity.rs` obey "A test lives with the code it tests". The deviation is not a deviation.
- No `unwrap`, `expect` or `panic!` on a non-test path in the added lines. No change to `*.png`, `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION`, `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock`, a golden `.cl` or `.cnc` file, or the pins `wall_arc_entry`, `lead_approach`, `shoulder_adaptive`. No new edge between our crates. Each new module has a provenance line. The decision file is present. The PR body has the readings, the pins, what was not exercised, `Changelog: none` and `Refs #917`. The commit also uses `Refs #917`. The app does not call `machining_mesh` yet, so `Changelog: none` is correct.

### Notes (not blockers)

1. **Snap after the measurement.** `measure_within` reads the plan before `weld` snaps the positions (`machining_mesh.rs:233` then `:266`). The final mesh can be up to `sqrt(3) * SNAP_WINDOW_MM` (1.73e-9 mm) farther from the surface than the judged bound. The three pins keep their margin after this. But a future reading within 1.73e-9 mm of the tolerance passes without proof. Recommended guard: compare `deviation.largest() + 3f64.sqrt() * SNAP_WINDOW_MM > tol_mm` at `machining_mesh.rs:237`, or add the term to `gated`. The decision text says "true to 1e-9 mm"; the true value is 1.73e-9 mm.
2. **Direction of the bound.** The bound is a bound of mesh-to-surface distance, as the `Deviation` docs say. The old parametric term (Hessian over the uv triangle) also bounded surface-to-mesh on that patch. `eps.min(side)` drops that second bound on the triangles where it acts. At a pole this is correct, because the patch is as small as the triangle. On a chart that folds back (corners near in 3D, the uv interior far in 3D), the surface could stand out of the mesh by more than the bound, and a toolpath on the mesh could gouge. Please state in the decision file that the gate is one-sided, or apply the `min` only where the uv triangle is near a degenerate point of the chart.
3. **Replan coverage.** No tracked fixture now passes only after a replan. The "replan, then pass" branch of `machining_mesh` has no pin. The bump case covers "replan, then refuse" only. A follow-up `P7` issue for a fixture is enough.
4. **Pinched vertex.** The snap can merge two vertices (at most 2e-9 mm apart) that share no triangle. The side count does not see a non-manifold vertex. The effect is at the picometre scale. Only a note.
5. **Stale ranges.** `Mesh.facets` and `Mesh.solids` are both `pub`. A caller that writes a new `facets` and keeps `solids` gets ranges that do not match. `slice_of` refuses only ranges out of bounds. PR B must keep the two fields in step, or make `solids` private.
6. **File length.** `crates/geometry/src/geometry/mod.rs` was at 477 lines and is now at 482. The PR makes a file that is already over 400 lines longer. Consider moving the `Mesh` items into `mesh_solids.rs` or a new `mesh.rs`.
7. **Guard gives no answer on bad data.** In `Spline::fault`, a bad multiplicity or a control point that is not a `CARTESIAN_POINT` returns `None` ("no fault") and stops the scan of that curve. The reader then reads the curve as before. This is no worse than before. A refusal would be clearer.

### Not checked

- No build, no test run, no clippy (read-only review). I used the author's readings: quick gate 948 steps and heavy gate 232 steps, 0 failed.
- I did not check `analytic_tri_bound` and `parametric_eps` in `mesh_bound.rs`. This PR does not change them.
- I did not measure the run time of the 2^21 sample budget on a large plan.
- I did not run the fixtures. I did not compare the three readings with an independent measurement.

Addressed (head eae027d5531d03d66176556149edf7a86a0b9623).

1. Inward turn, one shell only. `mesh_weld::turn_outward` turns the mesh only when `mesh_weld::shells` finds one shell (triangles joined side to side). A mesh of two or more shells with a negative volume stays the `Volume` refusal. New pins in `crates/kernel/tests/machining_mesh_parity.rs`:
   - `a_solid_with_a_void_and_its_outer_shell_inward_is_refused`: box.step with a half-size void (`BREP_WITH_VOIDS`, `ORIENTED_CLOSED_SHELL .F.`). With the outer shell outward it meshes at volume 0.875. With the outer shell inward it is refused by name. Today solidcore's reader refuses it first ("#16 at measure: ... not a positive finite solid measure ... volume: -0.875"). If a later reader lets it through, the test requires the mesher's `Volume` refusal.
   - `only_one_shell_is_ever_turned_outward`: two raw cube shells with a negative sum are not changed. One inward cube is turned.
2. Snap slack. The check now compares `deviation.largest() + SNAP_MOVE_MM` with the tolerance. `SNAP_MOVE_MM` = sqrt(3) x `SNAP_WINDOW_MM` = 1.73e-9 mm. The decision file says 1.73e-9 mm. The measured figures do not change; the judged figures (measured + 1.73e-9) of the three changed pins:

   | Fixture | Tolerance (mm) | Judged (mm) | Margin (mm) |
   |---|---|---|---|
   | Solidcraft sample | 0.005 | 0.0049999930 | 7.0e-9 |
   | Solidcraft sample | 0.1 | 0.0999999422 | 5.8e-8 |
   | fillet_corner.step | 0.005 | 0.0049998042 | 1.96e-7 |

   The three pins pass.
3. The decision file says that the adaptive bound is one-sided (mesh point to surface). The algorithm did not change.

Ran (CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=12):
- `cargo xtask gate test <name> --crate camcraft-kernel --binary machining_mesh --exact`, one at a time, for `solidcraft_sample_meshes_within_the_app_chord`, `solidcraft_sample_still_refuses_an_out_of_tolerance_mesh`, `machining_mesh_is_watertight_and_within_tolerance`, `a_bad_tolerance_or_a_spent_time_bound_is_refused_by_name`, `every_planner_shortfall_is_a_refusal_or_a_note`, `the_deviation_measure_sees_a_moved_node_and_a_wrong_surface`: all ok.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-kernel` for `--lib`, `machining_mesh_bounds` (4), `machining_mesh_parity` (7), `machining_mesh_shortfalls` (3, 1 ignored as before), `step_curve_guard` (4): all ok.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-kernel --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- No heavy lane: the delta does not change what a heavy lane reads, apart from a comparison that is 1.73e-9 mm stricter.

Read-only delta review (Opus). Not built here.

**Verdict for the whole PR at this head: Ready for the maintainer to merge.** The blocker of my review of `647d37204` is met. This verdict replaces my earlier verdict. The PR keeps `held-for-merge`: the maintainer merges it.

Delta read: `git diff 647d37204 eae027d55` (one commit, 4 files). No other file changed.

### Blockers

None.

### Checked

1. **One-shell turn (`mesh_weld.rs` `shells`, `turn_outward`).**
   - `shells` is a union-find over the triangles. Two triangles join when they use the same side. Each `parent` access uses `get` or `get_mut`, so the index math cannot panic. A union always links one root to a different root, so no cycle occurs and `root` ends.
   - An empty mesh gives 0 shells. `turn_outward` then returns `None`, and the `Volume` refusal stays.
   - Two shells that touch at one vertex count as 2. The mesh is not turned. That is the safe reading.
   - Two shells that share one side use that side 4 times. `sides()` refuses that mesh before the volume step.
   - A multi-shell mesh with a negative volume: `turn_outward` returns `None`, and `machining_mesh` returns `MeshRefusal::Volume`. Correct.
   - `only_one_shell_is_ever_turned_outward` pins the guard directly: two cubes with a negative sum stay unchanged, one inward cube is turned, and positive or NaN volumes stay unchanged. This is the pin that proves the guard.
   - `a_solid_with_a_void_and_its_outer_shell_inward_is_refused`: today the reader refuses the input first, so this test does not reach the mesher guard. It cannot pass for a wrong reason, because:
     - the same fixture with the outer shell outward must mesh at volume 0.875, which proves that the fixture builds;
     - the only difference between the two variants is the sense flags of the outer shell;
     - the accepted texts are specific ("#16" and "not a positive", or the mesher refusal with `Volume(v)` and `v < 0`).
     It is an end-to-end pin of "never accepted". The unit test above pins the guard.
2. **Snap slack.** `judged = deviation.largest() + SNAP_MOVE_MM` is used at the correct place: the accept or replan decision at `machining_mesh.rs:245-246`, before the weld. The constant is sqrt(3) x `SNAP_WINDOW_MM`, which is correct. NaN still refuses. The judged margins that the author gives (7.0e-9, 5.8e-8 and 1.96e-7 mm) are positive.
3. **Decision file.** It states that the bound is one-sided (mesh point to surface) and gives 1.73e-9 mm. It names the new pin.
4. **Code law.**
   - No `unwrap()`, `expect()` or `panic!` on a non-test path in the delta.
   - File lengths: `mesh_weld.rs` 136, `machining_mesh.rs` 341, `machining_mesh_parity.rs` 256.
   - No change to `*.png`, `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION`, Cargo files, goldens or the toolpath pins.

### Notes (not blockers)

1. **Reported figure.** The `Deviation` refusal reports `measured: deviation.largest()`, not `judged` (`machining_mesh.rs:255`). A plan with a reading in (tol - 1.73e-9, tol] is refused with a measured value that is not above the tolerance. That message can confuse. Report `judged`, or add the slack to the message.
2. **Refinement target.** `measure_within` still refines to `tol_mm` and not to `tol_mm - SNAP_MOVE_MM`. Refinement can stop at a bound that the new check then rejects, and that gives a replan or a refusal that is not necessary. This is conservative, not unsafe. Pass `tol_mm - SNAP_MOVE_MM` to `measure_within` if that occurs.
3. **Heavy lane.** I see no need for one. The delta makes the decision 1.73e-9 mm stricter and adds the shell guard. The only possible change is a fixture whose reading is within 1.73e-9 mm of its tolerance, which then replans. The author listed the readings of the three changed pins only. The post-merge gate or the cut gate will show any other fixture of this type.

### Not checked

- No build and no test run. I used the author's targeted gate on this head.
- I did not check that the solidcore reader refuses the void fixture with the text that the test accepts. I read the test only.

This PR is ready for the maintainer. No agent merges it: it has the label `held-for-merge`.

- Head: `eae027d5531d03d66176556149edf7a86a0b9623`. It merges cleanly with `main`.
- Review: the read-only Opus delta review has the marker for this head and found no blocker. It did not build the PR.
- Gates by the author: the quick gate (948 steps) and the heavy lanes (232 steps) passed on `647d37204`. On this head the author ran the touched kernel tests and clippy for `camcraft-kernel`. The reviewer saw no need for a new heavy run.
- Two notes of the review are not blockers: the Deviation refusal message shows the measured value and not the judged value, and `measure_within` refines to the tolerance without the snap margin.
- This PR takes no more pushes. The importer switch PR of #917 will stack on it.
